notes.text: Firmware - Pre-installed low-level software on hardware.
Term: BIOS; Full Form: Basic Input/Output System; Explanation: Initializes hardware and loads the OS.
Term: OS; Full Form: Operating System; Explanation: Software managing hardware and applications.
Component: CPU; Full Form: Central Processing Unit; Description: Brain of the computer, processes instructions.
Component: ALU; Full Form: Arithmetic Logic Unit; Description: Performs mathematical and logical operations.
Component: CU; Full Form: Control Unit; Description: Manages and controls CPU operations.
Component: RAM; Full Form: Random Access Memory; Description: Volatile memory; temporarily stores active processes.
Component: ROM; Full Form: Read-Only Memory; Description: Non-volatile memory; stores BIOS and firmware.
Component: HDD; Full Form: Hard Disk Drive; Description: Permanent storage; uses magnetic storage with moving parts.
Component: SSD; Full Form: Solid State Drive; Description: Faster storage with no moving parts; uses flash memory.
Component: GPU; Full Form: Graphics Processing Unit; Description: Renders images and graphics.
Component: PSU; Full Form: Power Supply Unit; Description: Powers all computer components.
Floppy - Capacity is 1.44MB (Now not in use)
Storage Type: HDD; Full Form (if any): Hard Disk Drive; Details: High capacity, slower than SSD, uses platters.
Storage Type: SSD; Full Form (if any): Solid State Drive; Details: Fast read/write speeds, no moving parts.
Storage Type: USB; Full Form (if any): Universal Serial Bus; Details: Portable plug-and-play storage.
Storage Type: CD/DVD; Full Form (if any): Compact Disc / Digital Versatile Disc; Details: Optical disk storage. A standard CD typically holds 700MB of data.
A standard single-layer DVD can hold 4.7GB of data.
Blu-ray Disc - High-capacity optical disc used for HD video and large data storage.
Storage Type: KB; Full Form (if any): Kilobyte; Details: 1024 Bytes.
Storage Type: MB; Full Form (if any): Megabyte; Details: 1024 KB.
Storage Type: GB; Full Form (if any): Gigabyte; Details: 1024 MB.
Storage Type: TB; Full Form (if any): Terabyte; Details: 1024 GB.
Bit - Smallest data unit.
Byte - 1 Byte = 8 bits
Nibble - 1 nibble =4 bits
Primary Memory - Main memory (RAM), used for temporary storage
Secondary Memory - Non-volatile storage (e.g., Hard Drive, SSD)
Cache Function - Fast-access storage used to speed up data retrieval Managed by Hardware
Dynamic RAM (DRAM) - Memory that needs to be refreshed regularly
Magnetic Storage Examples - Hard Disk Drives (HDD), Magnetic Tape
Register - Fast storage locations CPU. Their function is to store data and instructions that the CPU needs to access quickly. Managed directly by CPU.
Type: System Software; Examples: Windows 10/11, Linux Ubuntu, macOS, Android OS, iOS; Function: Manages computer hardware, provides basic functions, runs application software.

Type: Application Software; Examples: MS Word, MS Excel, Adobe Photoshop, VLC Media Player, Google Chrome, Zoom, Canva; Function: Helps users perform tasks like document creation, photo editing, browsing, media playing.

Type: Programming Software; Examples: Compilers: (Turbo C++, Dev C++, Code::Blocks, Eclipse, NetBeans, PyCharm, Visual Studio, GCC Compiler) Interpreters; Function: Provides tools for writing, debugging, and testing code. Used by developers for software creation.

Type: Utility Software; Examples: Avast Antivirus, CCleaner, WinRAR, Disk Defragmenter, Malwarebytes, Windows Disk Cleanup, Backup Software; Function: Performs system maintenance, optimizes performance, protects against malware.
Keyboard - Enters text and commands.
Mouse - Pointer control device.
Scanner - Converts physical documents to digital format.
Mic - Captures audio input.
Webcam - Captures video input.
Joystick - Controls games and simulations.
Monitor - Displays visual output.
Printer - Prints documents and images.
Speaker - Outputs sound.
Projector - Displays screen onto surface.
Headphones - Personal audio output.
Peripheral: Input Peripheral; Type: Input; Examples / Full Form: Keyboard, Mouse, Scanner
Peripheral: Output Peripheral; Type: Output; Examples / Full Form: Monitor, Printer, Speaker
Peripheral: Storage Peripheral; Type: Storage; Examples / Full Form: USB (Universal Serial Bus), External HDD, SSD
Port Types - USB, HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface), VGA (Video Graphics Array), LAN (Local Area Network), Audio Jack
Term: LAN; Full Form: Local Area Network; Explanation: Covers limited area like home or office.
Term: WAN; Full Form: Wide Area Network; Explanation: Covers large geographical area.
Term: IP Address; Full Form: Internet Protocol Address; Explanation: Unique identifier for a device on a network.
Term: Modem; Full Form: Modulator-Demodulator; Explanation: Converts digital signals to analog and vice versa.
Term: Wi-Fi; Full Form: Wireless Fidelity; Explanation: Wireless network access.
Term: ISP; Full Form: Internet Service Provider; Explanation: Provides internet services.
Term: MAC Address; Full Form: Media Access Control Address; Explanation: Hardware address of a network interface.
Protocol: HTTP; Full Form: Hypertext Transfer Protocol; Function: Used for transferring web pages over the internet.
Protocol: HTTPS; Full Form: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure; Function: Secure version of HTTP, encrypts data to prevent interception.
Protocol: FTP; Full Form: File Transfer Protocol; Function: Used for transferring files over the internet.
Protocol: IP; Full Form: Internet Protocol; Function: Responsible for addressing and routing data packets on the internet.
Protocol: TCP; Full Form: Transmission Control Protocol; Function: Ensures reliable transmission of data over the internet.
GUI (Graphical User Interface): Interface with icons and menus.
CLI (Command Line Interface): Text-based interface.
URL (Uniform Resource Locator): Address of a web page.
HTML (HyperText Markup Language): Web page coding language.
HTTP/HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol / Secure): Web communication protocols.
VPN (Virtual Private Network): Secure internet connection over public network.
OS (Operating System): Software managing the system.
IDE (Integrated Development Environment): Tool for writing and debugging code.
SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol): Protocol for sending emails.
POP3 (Post Office Protocol v3): Protocol for receiving emails.
IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol): Email retrieval protocol (cloud-based).
GIGO ("Garbage In, Garbage Out"): Concept that incorrect input results in incorrect output
MAC (Media Access Control): Unique identifier for network devices
VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration): A technology used to create integrated circuits (IC)
ANSI (American National Standards Institute): Sets standards for products, services, processes, systems
WinWord.exe - Executable file for Microsoft Word
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets): used for styling web pages

Generation: 1st Generation; Years: 1940- 1956; Technology Used: Vacuum Tubes; Languages Used: Machine Language; Examples: ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), UNIVAC (Universal Automatic Computer)
Generation: 2nd Generation; Years: 1956- T 1963; Technology Used: ransistors; Languages Used: Assembly Language; Examples: IBM 1401

Generation: 3rd Generation; Years: 1964- I 1971; Technology Used: Cs (Integrated Circuits); Languages Used: High-Level Languages (COBOL - Common Business-Oriented Language, FORTRAN - Formula Translation); Examples: IBM 360

Generation: 4th Generation; Years: 1971- Present; Technology Used: Microprocessors; Languages Used: C, C++, GUI (Graphical User Interface) Operating Systems; Examples: Intel 4004, IBM PC (Personal Computer)
Analog Computer - Works with continuous data. Example: Speedometers, Thermometers.
Digital Computer - Works with discrete data (binary). Examples: Personal computers, Smartphones.
Hybrid Computer - Combines features of analog and digital computers. Example: Medical devices.
Micro Computer - Small, general-purpose digital computers. Examples: Laptops, Desktops, PC
Main Frame Computers - Large-scale enterprise computing (e.g. banking)
Super Computer - Fastest, most powerful. Used in weather forecasting, scientific simulations, cryptography.
UNIVAC - Universal Automatic Computer
PDA - Personal Digital Assistant
Machine Language - Used for CPU-level instructions, hardware control.
Assembly Language - Used in embedded systems, device drivers.
C - Used in system programming, OS development.
C++ - Used in game development, software engineering, GUI applications.
Python - Used in AI, machine learning, automation, web development.
Java - Used in mobile apps, web applications.
JavaScript - Used for dynamic websites, web apps
Language: HTML; Full Form: HyperText Markup Language; Purpose / Usage: Used for web page structure, content formatting.
Computer - Derived from the Latin word computare meaning "to calculate"
Father of Computer - Charles Babbage
Modern Digital Computer Founder - Alan Turing (Father of Digital Computer)
First Electronic Digital Computer - John Vincent Atanasoff
Father of PC - Edward Robart
First Web Browser - WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus) - Developed by Tim Berners- Lee in 1990 at CERN (European Organization for Nuclear Research)
First Ever Programmer - Ada Lovelace
Compiler vs Interpreter - Compiler: Translates entire program at once; Interpreter: Translates line by line
Worm - Self-replicating malware; unlike viruses, it doesn't require a host program
Virus - Malware that attaches itself to a program or file and spreads when the program is executed
Diagnostic Software - Software used to troubleshoot issues (e.g., Disk Cleaners, AntiVirus)
Assembly - Low-level programming language
Cookies - Small pieces of data stored by a web browser to track users' activities
1. Malware - Software that is specifically designed to disrupt, damage, or gain
unauthorized access to a computer system.
E,g, viruses, worms, Trojans, spyware
Trojan Horse - Malware disguised as legitimate software
Melissa Email Virus (1999) - A virus that spread via email, causing severe disruption
Firewall - Firewalls act as a barrier to block unauthorized access to and from a network.
Anti-virus - Focuses on detecting and removing malicious software (malware) on a device
Encryption - Process of converting information into unreadable code to prevent unauthorized access
Cracking - Breaking into a system or program to bypass its security measures

Full Duplex Mode - Communication mode where data is transmitted in both directions simultaneously
ISDN - Integrated Services Digital Network; a digital phone network
IMEI - International Mobile Equipment Identity; unique identifier for mobile devices
Abacus - An ancient computing tool used for arithmetic operations

Logical Functions - For logical tests and conditions: IF → =IF(A1>10, "Yes", "No") returns "Yes" if A1 > 10, otherwise "No". AND ,OR , NOT etc
Text Functions - Work with text strings: CONCATENATE → =CONCATENATE(A1, " ", B1) combines texts. LEFT , RIGHT, LEN etc

Inkjet Printer - ▪฀ Uses liquid ink (dye or pigment-based) ▪฀ Resolution: 1200-4800 DPI (Dots per Inch) ▪฀ Ideal for color and photo printing ▪฀ Slower than laser; ink may dry if unused
Laser Printer - ▪฀ Uses dry toner and laser beam ▪฀ Resolution: 600-1200 DPI ▪฀ Fast and efficient for bulk printing ▪฀ Best for text documents (FASTEST)
Dot Matrix Printer - ▪฀ Uses ink ribbon + impact pins ▪฀ Resolution: 60-240 DPI ▪฀ Can print carbon copies ▪฀ Noisy, used in billing, industry
Thermal Printer - ▪฀ Uses heat-sensitive paper or ribbon ▪฀ Resolution: 200-300 DPI ▪฀ Quiet and fast ▪฀ Used in POS, receipts, shipping
LED Printer - ▪฀ Uses LED array (not laser) ▪฀ Resolution: 600-1200 DPI ▪฀ Low maintenance, compact ▪฀ Energy-efficient
Solid Ink Printer - ▪฀ Uses wax-like ink sticks ▪฀ Resolution: Up to 2400 DPI ▪฀ Produces vibrant color prints ▪฀ Needs warm-up; waxy finish
3D Printer - ▪฀ Uses PLA/ABS filament or resin ▪฀ Resolution: 100-300 microns (layer height) ▪฀ Creates 3D objects layer-by-layer ▪฀ Used in prototyping, medicine
Multifunction Printer - ▪฀ Combines printer, scanner, copier (+ fax) ▪฀ Inkjet or laser-based ▪฀ Ideal for home/office multitasks ▪฀ Cost-effective option
Plotter - ▪฀ Uses pens or inkjets for vector graphics ▪฀ High precision printing ▪฀ Used for CAD, maps, blueprints ▪฀ Prints on large formats
Thermal Transfer Printer - ▪฀ Uses heat + ribbon to transfer print ▪฀ Resolution: 200-600 DPI ▪฀ Produces durable labels; Important Details: ▪฀ Used in packaging, barcoding
